rule: Any language spindlebox maps must flow through every analysis function without changing that function. Language knowledge belongs to extraction (profiles as data, spindlebox/extract/, and typenorm/depmap resolution), which resolves it into neutral markers; analysis modules read only normalized fields.
gate: tests/test_language_agnostic.py scans every module under spindlebox/ except spindlebox/extract/ and spindlebox/generate/ for: a comparison on a `language`/`lang` name or attribute, a string literal naming a language (profile name, alias or file extension), `import builtins`, and any import of a `*_lang` extractor module. Every hit must match an entry below by module and hash.
hash: sha256 of the source of the smallest statement enclosing the hit, first 16 hex digits (ast.get_source_segment). Any edit to that statement changes the hash and voids the entry; the gate then fails until the edit is re-approved or the knowledge moves into extraction.
approval_protocol: An entry is added or re-hashed only in a fix-verify round, and the Codex verdict that accepts that round's commit is its approval; the `approval` object cites the cycle, contract, issue and round so the verdict is findable on the issue. A rejecting verdict means the entry must go: move the code into extraction or delete it. The seven analysis modules (gaps, workflows, validate, sigclass, ctxnorm, reporting, findings_model) may never hold an entry.

exceptions.statement: items = [i for i in items if i.language == args.lang]
exceptions.reason: `show --lang` is a user-supplied filter on the item's `language` field; no language is named in code, the value comes from the command line.
`search --lang` is a user-supplied filter on the item's `language` field; no language is named in code, the value comes from the command line.

Env-var detection regexes for the five natively-extracted languages. depmap is extraction-side resolution (the rule names it); profiled languages supply the same thing as `env_patterns` data, and these tables are the pre-profile remainder.
typescript reuses the javascript env-var regexes; extraction-side table aliasing.
tsx reuses the javascript env-var regexes; extraction-side table aliasing.

external_packages: Python import roots are classified against the interpreter's stdlib module list, which only the Python runtime can supply. Extraction-side resolution; the whole if/elif chain hashes as one statement.
external_packages: JavaScript/TypeScript package-name rules (scoped packages, node: and relative specifiers). Extraction-side resolution.
external_packages: Go module-path rule (a dotted first segment is a module host). Extraction-side resolution.
external_packages: Rust crate-root rule with the std/core/alloc builtin roots. Extraction-side resolution.
external_packages: Bash records every sourced path as external. Extraction-side resolution.
external_packages: profiled languages are looked up in the table their JSON profile registered (`external_imports`); a data lookup keyed by language, which is the pattern the rule wants.
`call` executes an item in-process and is Python-only by design; the check exists to refuse other languages with a clear error rather than exec a non-Python file.
`call` derives the synthetic module name from the Python file path it is about to exec_module; Python-only by design.
Body translation's per-target syntax table (Python source to Rust/Java spellings). translate is Python-only by design and the targets are output languages.
Body translation only reads Python source bodies, by design; the check refuses anything else rather than mistranslate it.
typenorm's per-language type normalizers for the natively-extracted languages; profiled languages register `types` tables from JSON instead. The rule names typenorm resolution as extraction-side.
typenorm: Bash has no type syntax, every value is a string. Extraction-side resolution (normalize()); the whole function body is one statement chain only at the `if` level, so this hashes alone.
typenorm: a `fixed`-mode profile registered its single type here; data lookup keyed by language.
typenorm: a `table`-mode profile registered its type table here; data lookup keyed by language.
typenorm: an unannotated slot is `any` in a dynamic language and `unit` in a typed one; the split is per-language knowledge that belongs to extraction and has no profile key yet.
